plain_summary: FILL during onboarding: two or three plain sentences that say what a great job looks like for this person. Every score is judged against this.

interests.description: Does the day-to-day work match what the candidate enjoys and is good at?
high_signals: FILL: kinds of work that energize the candidate
low_signals: FILL: kinds of work the candidate wants to avoid
interests.scoring_guide: 5 = the work is mostly what the candidate loves doing. 4 = mostly a good match with one minor drawback. 3 = a genuine mix. 2 = mostly work the candidate does not want. 1 = the wrong job entirely.

goals.description: Does the role move the candidate toward the career goal (title, level, company type and size)?
high_signals: FILL: titles, levels, company stages or sizes that fit the goal
low_signals: FILL: titles, levels or company types that move the wrong way
goals.scoring_guide: 5 = exactly the next step the candidate wants. 4 = a clear step forward with a small compromise. 3 = sideways. 2 = a step back or the wrong kind of company. 1 = nowhere near the goal.

location.description: Can the candidate actually get there, as often as the job asks?
location.scoring_guide: 5 = fully remote, or in the home area with a light office schedule. 4 = home area with a heavier schedule, or a nearby city with 1 to 2 office days a week. 3 = fully on-site in the home area, or a nearby city with 3 days. 2 = a nearby city with 4 or more days. 1 = would require moving.

comp.description: Does the posted pay meet the candidate's numbers? Pay is in the candidate's currency (see profile/candidate.json).
comp.scoring_guide: 5 = the posted range reaches the 'bonus' number or more. 4 = it reaches the floor but not the bonus. 3 = no pay posted (never a penalty). 2 = slightly under the floor. 1 = far under the floor.
comp.unlisted_policy: No pay posted scores 3 and sets comp_unknown. Missing pay is never held against a job.

overall.label: Dream fit
overall.description: The headline score, 1 to 5. Start from the weighted average of the four scores above using `weights`, then adjust by at most one point for things the four do not capture (a company the candidate has said they love, a stale posting, a red flag in the description). Be decisive: 3 means a true toss-up, not 'unsure'. A hard problem (an off-limits industry, a requirement the candidate clearly cannot meet) caps it at 2.

titles: FILL: job titles to search for
search_scope.geography: FILL: plain description, e.g. 'Remote in Canada, or hybrid in the Toronto area'
search_scope.sources_note: The sources that are switched on live in profile/candidate.json under sources.

hard_exclusions.employment_type: Skip part-time, internships, co-op, gig or freelance marketplaces, and contracts shorter than 12 months. Full-time contracts of 12 months or more are scored normally.
hard_exclusions.on_site: Fully on-site jobs outside the home area are skipped at intake (reason 'on-site'). Hybrid is never treated as on-site.
hard_exclusions.pay_floor: Skip a job whose posted pay tops out below dimensions.comp.floor (reason 'pay-floor'). Missing pay is NOT a reason to skip. Ignored while floor is 0.

research_gaps_rule: Before scoring, fill in missing facts that change the score (pay, office days, company size and stage, company website): check the company site, its careers page and the same posting on other job boards. Always read the description itself for a pay range before calling pay unknown. Only leave a fact unknown after actually looking, and say so in the rationale.

auto_apply.note: When enabled, each search puts jobs scoring min_overall or higher on the apply queue. Nothing is ever submitted until the candidate presses 'Apply queue now' on the dashboard.

worth_applying.label: Worth applying
worth_applying.description: A second score, 1 to 5, computed by scripts/score_worth_applying.py: how likely an application is to get a reply, based on years asked versus years the candidate has, required credentials, company size, match %, location and pay. It learns from real replies once there are enough of them.
worth_applying.weights_note: Empty means the defaults in scripts/score_worth_applying.py. Put a factor here to override it.
